parts.title: The Contradictions Of Tourism
parts.article:
(A) International tourism presents itself as straightforward, passive and benign, yet it is complex, interesting and important, full of contradictions and depths. It has enormous growth potential; almost every country desires an expansion in this sector. Yet whether and how to grow is not nearly as straightforward as one might hope.

(B) Tourism can provide the ideal export for developing countries, which can capitalize on their unique cultures and natural environments. However, to do this they need to have features such as airports, hotels, sanitation facilities, roads and medical facilities. A government can build these itself, using revenue from local taxes or getting finance from foreign lenders. Alternatively, the government may attract foreign investment, allowing others to pay for the building, thus relieving itself of providing capital but forgoing profits.

(C) Tourism is, however, a risky investment. It can gradually decline as a resort becomes seen as outdated, or it can be destroyed overnight by a single hurricane, or a political emergency. Even when successful, countries and localities are faced with a dilemma: keep it within limits, or extend its benefits but also deepen dependence on a single, fickle industry.

(D) By definition, tourists travel to see and knowingly to encounter the different, the original, the authentic. In this increasingly global world, what they want is regional and unique. But only through artifice can the tourist demand for authenticity be met. An event such as a festival or ceremony needs to be brought to their attention and its importance and unique nature elaborated to them. Natural sites, too, need to be presented if they are to be regarded as noteworthy; gates, permits, and notices are required to set them apart from the mundane. Complicated framing and staging allows tourists to recognize, by sight, "the actual thing".

(E) Tourism places a premium on the parts of a culture that are visible, such as handicrafts and costume, and disregards those that are not, like the rules governing seating on a bus, attitudes to the elderly, or appropriate ways of addressing family members; in this way, tourism favours what can be commodified. Yet commodities can be produced most efficiently using industrial machinery to take advantage of economies of scale, an option closed to village artisans. This alienates the producers from what is being produced, and means the product no longer has any personal meaning to them.

(F) In addition, cultural idiosyncrasies and natural spectacles change over time. Tourists can’t be attracted, however, to an unstable and ambiguous culture, or to a natural site that is in the process of transforming itself. As a consequence, efforts are made to fix and standardize: folk dances, tortilla-making, peace pipes, bird habitats and the course of the Amazon have all been bound and defined. Had they not been fixed, however, they would not be accessible.

(G) Tourism also promotes an external orientation. Like other exports, the "tourism experience" is produced by local people, and consumed by foreigners. To obtain loans and ultimately create revenue, a government of whatever size has to please outside investors and potential travelers. In these ways, tourism can result in a political system becoming more authoritarian and giving less consideration to the needs of individuals within the country.

(H) In recent years, with increased awareness of some of these dangers, the phenomenon of ecotourism has developed. This has been seen as a way to prevent and reverse the environmental degradation resulting from tourism as well as from general human activity. Ecotourists distance themselves from mainstream hotel tourists, and also from adventure tourists like those who have, for example, left rubbish at the base of Mount Everest in Nepal. They want to do things like sleep in tents on platforms in tropical rainforests, swim among the fish on coral reefs, or walk over a tree canopy on a net bridge. They value the ecosystem as it is and are willing to pay for its preservation. In this way, they create an incentive for local people to refrain from using natural resources for short-term gain.

(I) However, what is fortunate for the birds is not always so fortunate for the local people. In order to be environmentally sustainable, ecotourists have to be few in number. The economies of scale that allow tourism to be profitable cannot operate in a small bush camp. Camping doesn’t generate much revenue. Ecotourism proves that tourism does not have to be in conflict with environmental preservation. Unfortunately, it also proves that the realm in which the environment and the economy can be mutually supporting is tiny.

(J) Furthermore, Westerners’ interest in biodiversity often means that the tourist wants to listen to a parrot, not a local elder, and that dollars bypass beggars on their way to support trees. Thus ecotourists’ environmental awareness can stand in contrast to their indifference to the local human community. Tourism always contains a message: this is what we value, this is what we don’t.

Questions 27-31
List of words
Complete the summary using the list of words, A-J, below.
Tourism-an ideal export?
A developing country needs money to build things like roads, which provide the necessary for tourism. The country can use taxes from residents or from other countries to provide capital. Or, money can be found by using from abroad, which means the country will not receive any financial gain from what is built.
Tourism may be affected by natural disasters, political events and people’s of how modern the resort is. Even if the development of tourism is successful, a country has to decide whether the industry’s is desirable.
  • A accommodation
  • B investment
  • C feedback
  • D perceptions
  • E profit
  • F expansion
  • G loans
  • H industry
  • I infrastructure
  • J labour
Questions 32-35
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Q32 The writer says that for tourists, an authentic experience

  • A is only possible if official barriers can be removed.
  • B may be missed if people are not clear what they want.
  • C is created in an unnatural manner.
  • D may be destroyed by inappropriate behaviour.

Q33 The writer refers to the rules governing seating on a bus as an example of

  • A a way in which tourism may change the attitudes of local people.
  • B an unintentional cause of offence to local people by tourists.
  • C the wide variation there may be between different cultures.
  • D an aspect of culture which tourism tends to ignore.

Q34 Tourists’ interest in traditionally-made objects may lead to changes in

  • A how they are made.
  • B their design and function.
  • C tourist attitudes towards them.
  • D the way they are presented for sale.

Q35 The writer says that in order to promote tourism, features such as folk dances

  • A may be unintentionally neglected.
  • B have been publicised in undesirable ways.
  • C have been taught to people working in tourist areas.
  • D may be prevented from developing naturally.
Questions 36-40
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 3?
In boxes 36–40 on your answer sheet, write:

Q36 Ecotourism can be more profitable than mass tourism because it requires fewer facilities.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q37 Limiting the number of ecotourists is necessary to protect the environment.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q38 Some ecotourists prefer interacting with wildlife over engaging with local residents.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q39 Ecotourism always benefits both the local community and the environment equally.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q40 Tourism can influence a country’s political priorities.

  • A YES
  • B NO
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q27

解析 原文提到建机场、酒店和道路等，这些就是发展旅游业必需的“基础设施（infrastructure）”。

干扰 你可能想选A（住宿），但题目里明确提到了“道路（roads）”，道路属于基本建设，不能只用住宿来概括。

句子 However, to do this they need to have features such as airports, hotels, sanitation facilities, roads and medical facilities.

Q28

解析 原文说政府可以用当地税收，或者向外国出借人借钱（getting finance from foreign lenders），这直接对应选项里的“贷款（loans）”。

干扰 你可能想选B（投资），但原文这句话明确说的是向外国借钱，引入外资是在下一句才提到的另一种独立方案。

句子 A government can build these itself, using revenue from local taxes or getting finance from foreign lenders.

Q29

解析 原文说作为替换方案，政府可以吸引外国“投资（foreign investment）”来让别人支付建设费用。

干扰 你可能想选E（利润），但原文后半句说的是国家因为引入外资而“放弃利润（forgoing profits）”，所以从国外引入的只能是投资而不是利润。

句子 Alternatively, the government may attract foreign investment, allowing others to pay for the building, thus relieving itself of providing capital but forgoing profits.

Q30

解析 原文说如果度假村“被视为（seen as）”过时就会导致旅游业衰退，这对应人们对其现代程度的“看法和观念（perceptions）”。

干扰 你可能想选C（反馈），但“被视为过时”强调的是人们的主观感观和看法，而不是指实质性收集到的反馈意见。

句子 It can gradually decline as a resort becomes seen as outdated, or it can be destroyed overnight by a single hurricane, or a political emergency.

Q31

解析 原文说国家面临两难，是将其限制在一定范围内，还是扩大它的利益，这里的“扩大”对应产业的“扩张（expansion）”。

干扰 你可能想选E（利润），但原文说的是要不要继续扩大规模来获取更多好处，核心在这个产业要不要继续向外扩张。

句子 Even when successful, countries and localities are faced with a dilemma: keep it within limits, or extend its benefits but also deepen dependence on a single, fickle industry.

Q32

解析 原文指出只有通过人工手段（artifice）、复杂的构架和舞台布景，才能满足游客对“原汁原味”的需求，这说明体验是人为刻意制造出来的。

干扰 你可能想选B（错过体验因为不清楚想要什么），但原文明确表示游客非常清楚自己想要看地域性、独特的东西，并没有说他们不清楚需求。

句子 But only through artifice can the tourist demand for authenticity be met. An event such as a festival or ceremony needs to be brought to their attention and its importance and unique nature elaborated to them. Natural sites, too, need to be presented if they are to be regarded as noteworthy; gates, permits, and notices are required to set them apart from the mundane. Complicated framing and staging allows tourists to recognize, by sight, "the actual thing".

Q33

解析 原文直接说明旅游业会“无视（disregards）”那些看不见的文化，而公交车座位的规则就是作者给出的被无视的文化案例。

干扰 你可能想选C（不同文化的巨大差异），但这只是作者为了证明旅游业忽略某些特定文化而举出的具体例子，并不是为了长篇大论地讨论文化差异。

句子 Tourism places a premium on the parts of a culture that are visible, such as handicrafts and costume, and disregards those that are not, like the rules governing seating on a bus, attitudes to the elderly, or appropriate ways of addressing family members; in this way, tourism favours what can be commodified.

Q34

解析 原文提到旅游业看重手工艺品，导致现在最高效的生产方式变成了使用“工业机械（industrial machinery）”，这直接改变了它们的制造和生产方式。

干扰 你可能想选B（设计和功能），但原文强调的是从手工制作变成了工业机械批量生产，改变的是制作流程而不是物品本身的功能。

句子 Tourism places a premium on the parts of a culture that are visible, such as handicrafts and costume, and disregards those that are not... Yet commodities can be produced most efficiently using industrial machinery to take advantage of economies of scale, an option closed to village artisans.

Q35

解析 原文说文化本来是随时间自然改变的，但为了吸引游客，人们会把民间舞蹈等固定和标准化（fix and standardize），这就强行阻碍了它们的自然发展。

干扰 你可能想选B（以不良方式宣传），但原文强调的是把这些文化“定型”不让它们改变，并没有提到宣传方式好坏的问题。

句子 In addition, cultural idiosyncrasies and natural spectacles change over time. Tourists can’t be attracted, however, to an unstable and ambiguous culture, or to a natural site that is in the process of transforming itself. As a consequence, efforts are made to fix and standardize: folk dances, tortilla-making, peace pipes, bird habitats and the course of the Amazon have all been bound and defined.

Q36

解析 原文明确说生态旅游规模太小，产生不了多少收入（doesn't generate much revenue），这直接否定了它比大众旅游更赚钱的说法。

干扰 你可能主观觉得设施少就能省成本赚大钱，但原文白纸黑字写着这种小规模营地是无法实现规模经济去盈利的。

句子 In order to be environmentally sustainable, ecotourists have to be few in number. The economies of scale that allow tourism to be profitable cannot operate in a small bush camp. Camping doesn’t generate much revenue.

Q37

解析 原文直接说明，为了保持环境的可持续性（即保护环境），生态游客的数量“必须很少（have to be few in number）”。

干扰 你可能以为生态游客素质高就不需要限制人数，但原文非常直接地指出了人少是环保的必要前提条件。

句子 In order to be environmentally sustainable, ecotourists have to be few in number.

Q38

解析 原文提到游客宁愿听鹦鹉叫也不愿听当地老人说话，并指出他们对当地社区漠不关心（indifference），这就证明了他们更偏爱接触野生动植物。

干扰 你可能觉得生态游客道德高尚肯定也会关心当地穷人，但原文用鹦鹉和老人的对比直接揭开了他们无视当地人的真相。

句子 Furthermore, Westerners’ interest in biodiversity often means that the tourist wants to listen to a parrot, not a local elder, and that dollars bypass beggars on their way to support trees. Thus ecotourists’ environmental awareness can stand in contrast to their indifference to the local human community.

Q39

解析 原文明确指出，对鸟类（环境）幸运的事对当地人（社区）“未必幸运（not always so fortunate）”，直接反驳了两者均等获益的说法。

干扰 你可能看到“生态旅游”这个词就觉得它是完美的双赢，但原文一开始就强调了它对当地人并不总是有利的。

句子 However, what is fortunate for the birds is not always so fortunate for the local people.

Q40

解析 原文明确提到政府为了取悦外部投资者，可能会让政治体制（political system）变得更专制并较少考虑国民需求，这说明旅游业确实影响了国家的政治优先事项。

干扰 你可能认为旅游业只是一门单纯的经济生意，但原文直接点明了它会导致一个国家的政治系统和考虑重点发生实质性改变。

句子 To obtain loans and ultimately create revenue, a government of whatever size has to please outside investors and potential travelers. In these ways, tourism can result in a political system becoming more authoritarian and giving less consideration to the needs of individuals within the country.
